2306500.title: Ministry of Heavy Industries successfully observes Swachhata Pakhwada 2026 from 16th to 31st August 2026
2306500.body_html:
Ministry of Heavy Industries
Ministry of Heavy Industries successfully observes Swachhata Pakhwada 2026 from 16th to 31st August 2026
Shri Kamran Rizvi, Secretary, MHI, along with Ministry officials, took the Swachhata Pledge on 16th August 2026, reaffirming commitment to cleanliness and the vision of a Swachh Bharat
Shri Vijay Mittal, Joint Secretary, MHI, felicitated sanitation and support staff of the Ministry for their contribution to workplace cleanliness
A thorough cleanliness & plantation drive conducted during the campaign, in the areas of GPOA-3
An Essay Writing Competition to promote Swachhata and collective responsibility towards cleanliness organized in the Ministry
Various Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) & Autonomous Bodies(ABs) under the Ministry of Heavy Industries including BHEL, actively participated in Swachhata Pakhwada
Special Cleanliness drive also undertaken for bus-stop cleaning at Tiruchirappalli, a beach clean-up at Palavakkam Beach, Chennai, and railway-track cleaning at Hyderabad under MHI
Posted On: 03 SEP 2026 7:13PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) successfully observed Swachhata Pakhwada from 16th to 31st August 2026, as part of the Government of India’s Swachh Bharat Mission. The mission promotes cleanliness, hygiene, and sustainability across the nation. The two-week campaign followed the Calendar of Swachhata Pakhwada 2026 issued by the Government of India. This activity demonstrated MHI’s commitment to make cleanliness a shared duty and create a sustainable work environment.

The observance started with a pledge-taking ceremony on cleanliness by the officers and officials of MHI on 16th August 2026. Shri Kamran Rizvi, Secretary, MHI, administered the Swachhata Pledge to the Officers and Officials of MHI, reaffirming collective resolve to uphold cleanliness, and strengthen the spirit of Swachhata across workplaces and communities, thereby contributing to the vision of a Swachh Bharat.

Shri Kamran Rizvi, Secretary, Ministry of Heavy Industries administering ‘Swachhata Pledge’ to officers/officials of the Ministry

Shri Vijay Mittal, Joint Secretary, MHI, felicitated the sanitation and support staff of the Ministry in recognition of their dedicated services and valuable contribution towards maintaining cleanliness, hygiene and a clean workplace. Tokens of appreciation were presented to acknowledge their efforts and commitment, while recognising the dignity of work and the important role played by the support staff in fostering a clean and hygienic work environment.

Shri Vijay Mittal, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Heavy Industries, felicitated the dedicated sanitation and support staff

Throughout the fortnight, various activities were carried out to promote cleanliness and sustainability within the Ministry premises, including:

Cleanliness drives across all rooms, staircases, corridors, and common areas of GPOA-3.

Removalof unserviceable furniture, computers, printers, and other obsolete items to clear workspaces.

An essay competition on the theme ‘Swachh Bharat Abhiyan’ was organized on 21st August 2026 to reinforce the commitment towards creating a cleaner, healthier and more sustainable workplace, thereby contributing to the vision of a Swachh Bharat.

MHI organised an Essay Writing Competition to encourage awareness, participation and a sense of collective responsibility towards cleanliness and hygiene.

As part of Swachhata Pakhwada (16th–31st August, 2026), Bharat Heavy Electrical Limited (BHEL), a CPSE under the Ministry of Heavy Industries, across its manufacturing units, offices, project sites and establishments participated in various activities of Swachhata Pakhwada. During the campaign, BHEL carried out various activities such as cleanliness and housekeeping drives, removal and segregation of waste and scrap, cleaning of drains and common areas, revival and cleaning of rainwater harvesting systems, and internal audits covering STPs, ETPs, waste-management facilities, biomedical waste areas and storage systems. Special public cleanliness initiatives were also undertaken, including bus-stop cleaning at Tiruchirappalli, a beach clean-up at Palavakkam Beach, Chennai, and railway-track cleaning at Hyderabad. The Pakhwada concluded with Cleanathons, prize distribution and recognition of sanitation and housekeeping personnel, reaffirming BHEL’s commitment to cleanliness, environmental sustainability and collective responsibility in line with the vision of a Swachh Bharat.

BHEL carried out various activities across its manufacturing units, offices, project sites and establishments.

Other Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) and Autonomous Bodies (ABs) under the Ministry of Heavy Industries also actively participated in Swachhata Pakhwada from 16th to 31st August, 2026. The International Centre for Automotive Technology (ICAT), Manesar organised workplace and outdoor cleanliness drives, awareness activities on waste segregation, e-waste and reduction of single-use plastics, along with a Swachhata Quiz.

ICAT participated in Swachhata Pakhwada by undertaking a cleanliness drive across its centre.

NEPA Limited conducted cleanliness drives, plantation activities, cleanliness audits and housekeeping competitions. Bridge and Roof Company (India) Limited (B&R) undertook cleanliness drives across offices and project sites, tree plantation, e-waste and scrap disposal and awareness activities.

NEPA participated in a cleanliness drive and collective shramdaan at the Administrative Building, reaffirming their commitment to a clean, hygienic and responsible workplace

Hindustan Salts Limited (HSL) focused on workplace cleanliness, sanitation, waste management, plantation, fire-safety and digital cleanliness. Instrumentation Limited organised awareness rallies, painting competitions, cleanliness drives and sanitation improvement activities, while HMT Limited conducted cleanliness and beautification drives, waste segregation, e-waste disposal, plantation and awareness programmes. National Automotive Board (NAB) observed Swachhata Pakhwada with pledge-taking, awareness programmes, competitions and cleanliness drives. Awareness activities and a painting competition were also organised for school students, promoting cleanliness, hygiene and environmental responsibility.

A plantation drive was conducted at the premises of Instrumentation Limited

The successful observance of Swachhata Pakhwada 2026 reaffirmed the MHI’s commitment to the Swachh Bharat Mission and the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047. Through collective efforts of employees of MHI and its CPSEs/ABs, the Ministry promoted cleanliness, sustainability and collective responsibility, contributing towards a cleaner, greener, healthier and more developed India, ensuring a sustainable future for generations to come.

2306490.title: National Pledge Against Drug Abuse To Commemorate  The 6th Anniversary Of The Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan
2306490.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
National Pledge Against Drug Abuse To Commemorate  The 6th Anniversary Of The Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan
More Than 34.56 crore Crore Citizens including over 13.71 Crore youth and 10.65 Crore women Reached Under Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Through Nationwide Awareness Campaigns
NMBA e-Pledge On https://nashamukt.dosje.gov.in/epledge
Posted On: 03 SEP 2026 7:09PM by PIB Delhi

The National Mass Pledge Against Drug Abuse has been scheduled this month to mark the 6th anniversary of the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA).

The Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is the Nodal Ministry that aims to mobilise 10 Crore+ citizens through both physical and online participation.

In this connection, two high-level coordination meetings chaired by Joint Secretary (Drug Prevention) in the Ministry Dr. Sandeep Rewaji Rathod, held today in national capital, discussed the plan and the comprehensive strategy to ensure the participation of the target number of citizens in nationwide pledge through physical and online mode in line with the objectives of Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan.

The meetings were also attended by Director, DoSJE (DP) Shri Astik Kumar Pandey, Under Secretary Shri Arun Kumar Karn, besides other officials of the Ministry.

The meetings attended by the senior representatives from various ministries and departments, reviewed the ongoing work for the implementation strategy. The role of Line Ministries and Departments was discussed in mobilising officers, officials, students, parents, volunteers and other stakeholders for the nationwide pledge.

The meetings discussed organising pledge ceremonies across all affiliated offices, educational institutions, autonomous bodies, PSUs and field formations under respective Ministries and Departments including Railways, Defence, Civil Defence, Youth Affairs & Sports, School & Higher Education, Post, Police, CAPF, NCC, AYUSH, Rural Development, Health & Family Wefare Revenue besides social, voluntary, spiritual organizations and social influencers.

The Uniform Reporting Mechanism for submission of participation details and outreach, was also discussed in the meeting.

A power point presentation on the plan and coordinated strategy, was discussed threadbare which witnessed active deliberations by all the representatives from the Line Departments and the Ministries.

NMBA Pledge is an initiative to volunteer for reaching out to the victims of substance abuse. The pledge aims to encourage responsible behaviour to instil a sense of responsibility among people to stay away from drugs, to promote and foster sense of Unity and Commitment for encouraging stakeholders to work together towards a common goal. The Pledge further seeks to empower youth to contribute actively to developing a drug-free society.

The link of the NMBA e-Pledge is: https://nashamukt.dosje.gov.in/epledge

The meeting also highlighted to focus on the significant message to promote and encourage Drug De-addiction through Helpline—14446.

 

The meeting focussed on the evolving spirit among citizens to act as volunteers by registering as Nasha Mukti Mitr through Department’s official website:

https://nashamukt.dosje.gov.in/nasha-mukti-mitr

The Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment launched the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA) on 15th August 2020 to combat drug demand in the country. Recognising the urgent need for collective action, the Ministry coordinates various initiatives including prevention, assessment, treatment, rehabilitation, aftercare, public information dissemination, and community awareness.

The Ministry is implementing a comprehensive and evidence-based strategy under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR). The strategy is based on the findings of the first National Survey on the Extent and Pattern of Substance Use in India conducted by National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre (NDDTC) at AIIMS, New Delhi.

Under NAPDDR, the Ministry provides financial assistance to State Governments, Union Territories, NGOs and Government hospitals for preventive education, awareness generation, counselling, treatment and rehabilitation.

As on date, the campaign has reached more than 34.56 crore citizens including over 13.71 Crore youth and 10.65 Crore women, through nationwide awareness activities. More than 1.64 Lakh Nasha Mukti Mitras (NMM) have also joined the campaign to strengthen community participation.

The NMBA Portal is https://www.dosje.gov.in/organisation/nasha-mukt-bharat-abhiyaan/

To improve accessibility to treatment services, the Ministry has launched the NMBA 2.0 Mobile Application enabling citizens to locate the nearest de-addiction centre.

 

The App can be downloaded from the Google Play Store via this Link: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.dosje.nmba_app&hl=en_IN

The Government continues to strengthen its commitment towards a drug-free and socially inclusive India by expanding rehabilitation infrastructure, enhancing preventive interventions, simplifying implementation procedures and ensuring efficient delivery of Centrally Sponsored Schemes. Through sustained community participation, improved governance and technology-enabled service delivery, the Ministry remains committed to protecting vulnerable communities and promoting social justice for all.

2306481.title: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Reviews SHG-Bank Linkages, Lays Out Credit Roadmap for Women Entrepreneurs
2306481.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Reviews SHG-Bank Linkages, Lays Out Credit Roadmap for Women Entrepreneurs
Faster, Adequate and Accessible Credit for Women Entrepreneurs: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Women’s Empowerment Is Essential to Building a Developed India: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
From 3 Crore to 6 Crore Lakhpati Didis: Chouhan Pledges to Deliver PM Modi’s Vision
₹10 Lakh Crore for SHGs, ₹1 Lakh Crore for Individual Women Entrepreneurs in Five Years: Shri Chouhan
Quarterly Virtual, Half-Yearly Physical Reviews to Ensure Time-Bound Delivery: Shri Chouhan
Train, Sensitise and Deliver: Chouhan Pushes Banks to Improve Credit Access for SHG Women
Private Bankers Must Ensure Participation in District-Level Coordination Meetings: Chouhan
Posted On: 03 SEP 2026 6:56PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan chaired a high-level meeting in Mumbai on Thursday to review Self-Help Group-bank linkages and individual enterprise financing under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM). The meeting laid out a concrete roadmap for ensuring faster, adequate and accessible credit for women entrepreneurs, while also directing the setting up of a helpline to address difficulties faced by SHG members in accessing bank loans. SHG women, bankers, officials of State Rural Livelihood Missions, representatives of the Reserve Bank of India, National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development and other stakeholders participated in the meeting and held detailed discussions on bottlenecks in the loan process, regional disparities and possible solutions.


The high-level meeting focused on reviewing data, addressing ground-level challenges faced by SHG members, including delays in loan approvals, paperwork, low credit limits and difficulties at the branch level.

Union Minister of State for Rural Development and Communications Dr Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Minister of State for Rural Development Shri Kamlesh Paswan, Maharashtra Minister for Rural Development and Panchayati Raj Shri Jaykumar Gore and Minister of State Shri Yogesh Kadam, Secretary, Department of Rural Development, Shri Rohit Kansal, Joint Secretaries Shri Amit Kumar Shukla and Smt Swati Sharma, and other senior officials of the Rural Development Department were present. Representatives from the Department of Financial Services, NITI Aayog, RBI, NABARD and the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) also attended the meeting.

Women’s Empowerment Central to the Vision of a Developed India

Addressing the meeting, Shri Chouhan said women’s empowerment was a fundamental prerequisite for building a developed India. Referring to PM Shri Narendra Modi’s vision, Shri Chouhan said that from the Red Fort this year, the Prime Minister had reiterated the commitment to increase the number of Lakhpati Didi from three crore to six crore. Shri Chouhan urged all stakeholders to place the national interest above individual interests and make a sense of duty their defining characteristic. “We are not doing this merely as a profession or simply for a livelihood. Whether our officers or our friends associated with banks, we have a commitment to serve the country and serve the people. We are working to fulfil that commitment,” he said. He called upon all stakeholders to become emotionally invested in achieving the target. “There should be a determination, passion and enthusiasm within us that we have to change the lives of our sisters. We must constantly ask ourselves how our contribution can be the best and how we can do better. If we make that effort, we will certainly achieve the target faster,” he said.

From 3 Crore to 6 Crore Lakhpati Didi

Shri Chouhan said that achieving the first target of three crore Lakhpati Didis was relatively easier because many women were already earning ₹60,000, ₹70,000 or ₹80,000. “But now that we have to reach six crore, we will also have to make women earning ₹40,000, ₹50,000 or ₹30,000 Lakhpati Didis,” he said. The Union Minister appreciated the performance of bankers and said the progress achieved so far was a matter of pride. “What we have achieved is truly something to be proud of. Almost every bank has achieved one-and-a-half times its target this year, and some have even achieved twice their target. I extend my heartfelt congratulations for this. But going forward, we will have to come together again with the same passion and commitment,” he said.


Time-Bound Monitoring of Commitments

Shri Chouhan directed all stakeholders to ensure that the commitments made during the meeting were implemented with full capacity and within defined timelines. He announced that the stakeholders would meet virtually once every three months and hold a physical meeting every six months to ensure continuity and monitor progress. “If there is continuity in our meetings, we will certainly be able to adhere to the timelines as well,” Shri Chouhan said.

Training and Sensitisation at Bank Level

Highlighting the difficulties faced by SHG women at the banking level, Shri Chouhan called for greater training and sensitisation among bank officials. “You have seen that the biggest problems faced by our sisters arise at the bank level. We have to make efforts towards training and sensitising people at that level,” he said. He called for regular SRLM meetings with active participation from banks. “In particular, I have received complaints that private bankers are often absent from these meetings and from District Level Consultative Committee (DLCC) meetings. They too must make every effort to fulfil this commitment with seriousness,” he said.

Greater Focus on Poorer Regions

Shri Chouhan stressed that areas with higher levels of poverty must receive greater attention. “Many times, more money goes to places where prosperity already exists. Bank branches provide loans more quickly there. But where the need is greater, our focus should be there. ‘Let us light the lamp where darkness still exists.’ Those must certainly be our focus areas,” he said.

‘Atmavat Sarvabhuteshu’: An Emotional Commitment to the Goal

Urging stakeholders to connect emotionally with the mission, Shri Chouhan invoked the Indian ethos of ‘Atmavat Sarvabhuteshu’ — treating the suffering of others as one’s own. “We believe in ‘Atmavat Sarvabhuteshu’. We are all part of the same consciousness. Why should anyone remain unhappy? Why should their suffering not become our own suffering? ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’, the welfare of the world and ‘Sarve Bhavantu Sukhinah’ are the fundamental values of our culture,” he said. “If we internalise that spirit and work towards achieving this goal, we will truly find joy in our work,” he added. Congratulating all stakeholders for their efforts, Shri Chouhan said the next step was to focus on a clear roadmap, defined timelines and effective implementation. “We have to work towards achieving the bigger goal with a clear roadmap and timeline, and make every effort to achieve it within that timeframe,” he said.


No Target Is Impossible

Quoting renowned Bhopal-based Hindi poet Dushyant Kumar, Shri Chouhan said no target was beyond reach if there was determination and sustained effort. “Let us resolve that we will fulfil the commitments we have made. We will achieve the targets and goals we have set and fulfil the Prime Minister’s commitment within the stipulated timeframe,” Shri Chouhan said.

Over 10 Crore Rural Women Mobilised, ₹13.67 Lakh Crore Credit Extended

Under DAY-NRLM, more than 10 crore rural women have so far been organised into 92–93 lakh Self-Help Groups. Banks have extended cumulative credit of more than ₹13.67 lakh crore to SHGs. Shri Chouhan said that approximately 3.5 crore Lakhpati Didi had been created so far, against the target of six crore. Over the next five years, the government has set a target of making ₹10 lakh crore in loans available to SHGs and ₹1 lakh crore in loans to individual women members.

Action Plan for Financial Inclusion 2.0

The discussions held at the meeting will feed into the future action plan under the Financial Inclusion 2.0 vision. The initiative will focus on timely and adequate credit for SHGs, dedicated financing for women entrepreneurs and expanding access to high-quality financial services across rural India. Shri Chouhan assured that every possible step would be taken to ensure that SHG women do not face difficulties in accessing bank loans. A helpline, process improvements and continuous coordination with bankers will be used to identify and remove bottlenecks. The meeting is expected to serve as an important step towards strengthening women-led rural development, deepening financial inclusion and promoting inclusive economic growth across rural India.

2306465.title: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda inaugurates Centre for Advanced Bladder Diagnostics and PET-CT & SPECT-CT facilities at VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital
2306465.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2306465.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda inaugurates Centre for Advanced Bladder Diagnostics and PET-CT & SPECT-CT facilities at VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital
Centre for Advanced Bladder Diagnostics integrates Video Urodynamics (VUDS) with Near Infrared Spectroscopy (NIRS) -based brain mapping; first such approach being attempted in India
New diagnostic facilities to benefit approximately 5,600 patients annually at affordable cost
Posted On: 03 SEP 2026 6:30PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare, Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, today inaugurated the Centre for Advanced Bladder Diagnostics in the Department of Urology and the PET-CT and SPECT-CT facilities in the Department of Nuclear Medicine at VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital, New Delhi.

During his visit, Shri J.P. Nadda also visited the Heart Command Centre and the Sports Injury Centre at Safdarjung Hospital and reviewed the services and activities being undertaken at these centres.

During the detailed review of the functioning and ongoing projects of Safdarjung Hospital, Shri J.P. Nadda emphasised the need for regular review of projects and periodic inspection of projects in the pipeline. He stressed the importance of setting practical and achievable timelines for completion of projects to ensure their timely implementation. The Union Health Minister also appreciated the distinct identity and reputation that Safdarjung Hospital has established over the years and noted that the institution has developed its own unique name and standing in the healthcare sector.

Centre for Advanced Bladder Diagnostics

The Centre for Advanced Bladder Diagnostics has been established with Video Urodynamics (VUDS) integrated with Near Infrared Spectroscopy (NIRS). The facility will enable detailed assessment of bladder function and support diagnosis of urinary bladder disorders, including complex cases associated with neurological conditions.

An important feature of the Centre is the integration of VUDS with brain mapping through NIRS, an approach being attempted for the first time in India. It enables assessment of changes in cerebral blood oxygenation during bladder filling and emptying and may assist clinicians in determining whether a bladder disorder is of bladder-related, neurological or combined origin.

The Centre is expected to cater to approximately 5,000 patients annually, thereby strengthening the availability of specialised urological diagnostic services at the hospital.

PET-CT and SPECT-CT facilities

The newly installed PET-CT and SPECT-CT facilities in the Department of Nuclear Medicine will augment the hospital’s diagnostic capabilities in several specialised areas, including cancer care, cardiology, neurology, renal diseases and endocrinology.

The PET-CT facility will support cancer diagnosis, staging, treatment planning and follow-up, besides facilitating advanced imaging required for specialised therapies. It will further support multidisciplinary clinical management involving Medical Oncology, Radiation Oncology, Hematology, Urology, Nephrology and Pediatric Oncology.

The SPECT-CT facility will strengthen diagnostic services for cardiac, renal, endocrine, orthopaedic and gastrointestinal conditions, thereby facilitating comprehensive diagnostic evaluation and appropriate clinical management. The advanced Nuclear Medicine services are expected to benefit approximately 600–700 patients annually and will be made available at an affordable cost.

The addition of these services marks a further strengthening of the specialised healthcare infrastructure at VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital. The Centre for Advanced Bladder Diagnostics, PET-CT and SPECT-CT services will facilitate comprehensive diagnostic evaluation, support timely treatment planning and further strengthen multidisciplinary patient care.

The facilities will also support postgraduate education and training, while enhancing access to specialised diagnostic and therapeutic services for patients, including those belonging to economically disadvantaged sections of society.

The programme was held in the presence of Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Secretary, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare; Dr. Kavita Rani Sharma, Director, VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital; Dr. Charu Bamba, Medical Superintendent, Safdarjung Hospital; and Smt. Chitra, Joint Secretary (Hospital), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare. Senior officers of the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare and faculty members of VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital were also present.

2306458.title: NFDC-NFAI and FTII to Organise Specialised Workshop on Moving Image Preservation, Archiving, Digitization and Restoration
2306458.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
NFDC-NFAI and FTII to Organise Specialised Workshop on Moving Image Preservation, Archiving, Digitization and Restoration
Posted On: 03 SEP 2026 6:15PM by PIB Mumbai

Mumbai/Pune, 3 September 2026

 

The NFDC-National Film Archive of India (NFDC-NFAI), in association with the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune, will organise a specialised workshop on “Moving Images: Preservation, Archiving, Digitization and Restoration” from October 5 to 15, 2026, excluding weekends, at the NFDC-NFAI and FTII campuses in Pune.

The workshop is designed for students, aspiring professionals, researchers and others interested in film preservation, archiving, restoration, film technology and audiovisual heritage. It will provide participants with an understanding of the art, science and practice of preserving moving images through classroom sessions, practical demonstrations, hands-on training, institutional visits and screenings of archival and restored films.

The programme will cover important areas including moving image preservation, metadata, digital preservation, film types and bases, preventive conservation, digital film restoration, paper conservation and audio restoration. Practical sessions will include film identification, inspection and repair, manual film cleaning, celluloid and digital film projection, film scanning and digitization. Participants will also learn about film scanners, picture and audio scanning, storage requirements, colour grading and quality control.

Participants will get first-hand exposure to the working environment and facilities of NFDC-NFAI, including its Library and Vaults, Documentation and Projection Room. The workshop will also provide exposure to professional restoration workflows with support from Prasad Corp., which will contribute its technical expertise and equipment for film repair, conservation and digital restoration.

The programme will include institutional visits to NFDC-National Film Archive of India, FTII, Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute and Reserve Bank of India Archives. These visits will familiarise participants with different approaches to preservation, documentation, conservation and management of archival collections.

An international perspective will be provided through a dedicated session on practices followed by the Thai Film Archive. Archival and restored film screenings, including presentations on 35mm and digital formats, will also form an important part of the programme.

Speaking on the initiative, Shri Dhiraj Singh, Vice-Chancellor, FTII, said the programme brings together film education and preservation of cinematic heritage and will provide participants with academic learning, practical exposure and access to specialised facilities.

Shri Prakash Magdum, Managing Director, NFDC, said the initiative aims to share institutional experience and specialised skills with students and aspiring professionals and encourage greater interest in film preservation.

Shri Abhishek Prasad, Director & CTO, Prasad Corp., said the collaboration will help nurture the next generation of preservation professionals by sharing industry experience and technology.

The course will be led by Aparna Subramanian, Course Director, with a maximum intake of 24 participants. The course fee is ₹12,000 per participant.

Interested candidates may contact FTII at 020-2553 0085 or write to info.cfol@ftii.ac.in / fro@ftii.ac.in for registration and further details.

2306438.title: EPFO urges eligible establishments to settle long-pending EPF damages disputes at substantially reduced rates under VISHWAS, 2026
2306438.body_html:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
EPFO urges eligible establishments to settle long-pending EPF damages disputes at substantially reduced rates under VISHWAS, 2026
High Courts endorse the Scheme, encourage establishments to avail benefits
Posted On: 03 SEP 2026 5:54PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has launched VISHWAS, 2026, a one-time settlement scheme that allows employers to close long-pending disputes by paying a sharply reduced penalty amount.The Scheme will remain open until 28 December 2026. Employers are encouraged to apply within this period, as the closing date will not be extended.

Under normal rules, the penalty for late PF deposit can be as high as 37% per year. Under VISHWAS, 2026, the penalty has been reduced as follows:

  • Delay for up to 2 months: pay only 0.25% per month,
  • Delay from 2 to 4 months: pay only 0.50% per month,
  • Delay beyond 4 months: pay only 1% per month.

The Hon'ble Bombay High Court (Pune Bench), in WP No. 4246 of 2018, ordered an employer to apply under VISHWAS, 2026 within two weeks, modified the earlier tribunal order accordingly, and disposed of the writ petition. The Hon'ble Madras High Court disposed of WP No. 38008 of 2024 the moment the employer expressed willingness to avail the Scheme, closing the writ petition and related tribunal proceedings simultaneously. The Hon'ble Kerala High Court (Ernakulam Bench) has gone a step further and issued similar directions in nineteen separate cases, directing those establishments to approach EPFO and settle under VISHWAS, 2026.

In a significant relief measure for employers, cases relating to delayed payment of Provident Fund (PF) contributions prior to 14 June 2024 may be considered under the applicable provisions, provided the employer falls within specified categories. The coverage includes cases where proceedings relating to penalties are currently pending before a court or tribunal; cases where the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has already passed a penalty order but recovery, either fully or partially, is still pending; cases where EPFO has issued a notice proposing the imposition of a penalty but a final order has not yet been passed; and cases where EPFO records reflect delays in PF payments but no penalty notice has been issued so far.

The entire process has been made available through an online mechanism. Employers are required to first clear all outstanding interest on delayed PF contributions before submitting an application. Thereafter, they may log on to the EPFO Employer Portal at https://unifiedportal-emp.epfindia.gov.in, access the VISHWAS, 2026 module, select the applicable category, upload the required documents and complete the process through digital authentication.

The system will automatically calculate the revised penalty amount. Employers will be provided 15 days to make the payment, with an automatic extension of a further 15 days, wherever required. Upon confirmation of payment, EPFO will issue a digitally signed Settlement Certificate, following which the concerned proceedings pending before a court or tribunal shall stand closed.

Employers are encouraged to avail the benefits of the Scheme before its closure on 28 December 2026. Assistance is available at all 153 EPFO Regional Offices across the country, where dedicated VISHWAS Cells and Helpdesks have been established to facilitate and assist applicants. Detailed guidelines and Frequently Asked Questions are available on the EPFO website. For further assistance, employers may also contact the toll-free helpline at 1800-180-1820.

2306424.title: Occupational Safety Training under NAMASTE Scheme Inaugurated in West Bengal: First Batch Begins for Sanitation Workers of Durgapur Municipal Corporation
2306424.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Occupational Safety Training under NAMASTE Scheme Inaugurated in West Bengal: First Batch Begins for Sanitation Workers of Durgapur Municipal Corporation
Five Day Programme to Promote Safe Practices and Mechanised Sanitation; West Bengal Profiles 7,630 Sewer and Septic Tank Workers
We need to provide sanitation workers with a safe, dignified and mechanised working environment: Smt. Agnimitra Paul
Posted On: 03 SEP 2026 5:46PM by PIB Delhi

The Occupational Safety Training Programme under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme was inaugurated in West Bengal, with the first batch commencing for sanitation workers of the Durgapur Municipal Corporation.

The programme was organised under the NAMASTE Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, with technical support from the CSIR-Central Mechanical Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-CMERI).

The programme was inaugurated in the presence of Smt. Agnimitra Paul, Minister-in-Charge, Urban Development and Municipal Affairs, Government of West Bengal.

Senior officials and representatives from CSIR-CMERI, the State Urban Development Agency, Asansol Municipal Corporation, Durgapur Municipal Corporation and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) also attended the programme.

Addressing the gathering, Smt. Agnimitra Paul highlighted the importance of providing sanitation workers with a safe, dignified and mechanised working environment. She reiterated the commitment to eliminating hazardous cleaning practices through training, appropriate safety equipment and increased adoption of mechanised sanitation solutions.

Smt. Agnimitra Paul appreciated the support extended by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, NSKFDC and CSIR-CMERI in strengthening the safety and capacity of sanitation workers in West Bengal. She emphasised that sanitation workers perform an essential role in keeping cities clean and healthy, and that safeguarding their dignity, safety and well-being is a collective responsibility.

West Bengal has completed the profiling of 7,630 Sewer and Septic Tank Workers. Personal Protective Equipment kits have also been distributed among identified workers. Awareness workshops on preventing hazardous sanitation practices have been conducted across 124 municipalities and three cantonment boards in the State.

To strengthen emergency preparedness, the blood-group details of sanitation workers have been collected and an emergency database has been created to facilitate timely assistance during critical situations.

Identity Cards were also distributed to sanitation workers during the programme. The initiative recognises sanitation workers as an integral part of the urban sanitation ecosystem and reinforces the dignity and importance of their work.

Safaimitras from the Durgapur Municipal Corporation participated in the programme. An audio-visual safety walk demonstrating the importance and correct use of Personal Protective Equipment was presented. The dignitaries also visited the Swachh Bharat Test Bed and the training facility for Safaimitras developed by CSIR-CMERI.

The Occupational Safety Training programme will be conducted over five days and comprise 30 hours of instruction. Each batch will accommodate a maximum of 45 sanitation workers.

An assessment will be conducted after completion of the training. Participants maintaining at least 70 per cent attendance will receive a certificate and a stipend of Rs 1,000.

The training will enhance the knowledge and practical skills of sanitation workers in occupational safety, appropriate use of Personal Protective Equipment, safe working practices, emergency response and mechanised sanitation operations.

In the first phase, the training programme is being implemented in Durgapur Municipal Corporation, Asansol Municipal Corporation, Bardhaman Municipality, Bidhannagar Municipal Corporation and Chandannagar Municipal Corporation. It will subsequently be expanded to other municipalities in the State in a phased manner.

As part of the initiative, CSIR-CMERI is proposed to serve as a one-stop institutional centre for sanitation-worker safety and mechanisation. It will provide an integrated platform for occupational safety training, testing and assessment of safety equipment, and verification of equipment and devices used in sanitation operations.

The institutional mechanism will promote the adoption of appropriate and reliable safety equipment by facilitating systematic testing against relevant technical and safety requirements. It will also support the capacity-building of sanitation workers and other stakeholders through structured technical and practical training.

By bringing together training, technology, testing and equipment verification under one institutional framework, the initiative will help Urban Local Bodies make informed decisions concerning safety equipment and mechanised sanitation solutions.

The NAMASTE Scheme promotes the safety, dignity and socio-economic well-being of sanitation workers while supporting the mechanisation of sanitation work and elimination of hazardous cleaning practices.

The Scheme seeks to ensure that sanitation workers are not required to undertake hazardous manual entry into sewers or septic tanks. Urban Local Bodies, government and private organisations, contractors and other agencies engaged in sanitation operations are expected to follow prescribed safety procedures and adopt mechanised solutions.

The programme reaffirmed the commitment of the Government of India and the Government of West Bengal to building a safer, mechanised and dignified sanitation ecosystem.

Safety, dignity and mechanisation remain the three foundational pillars of the NAMASTE Scheme.

2306423.title: India and Belgium call for deeper defence industrial collaboration to build stronger militaries through co-development & co-production
2306423.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
India and Belgium call for deeper defence industrial collaboration to build stronger militaries through co-development & co-production
Posted On: 03 SEP 2026 5:45PM by PIB Delhi

Minister of Defence & Foreign Trade of Belgium Mr Theo Francken has emphasised the strong potential for deeper industrial collaboration between India and Belgium to strengthen the defence forces through collective efforts, with Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth urging Belgian defence manufacturers to leverage their technological expertise alongside India’s manufacturing scale for co-development & co-production of niche products for shared security and prosperity. The two Ministers graced the India-Belgium Defence CEOs Roundtable and B2B Meetings in New Delhi on September 03, 2026.  The event was attended by the representatives of the Belgian industry, Confederation of Indian Industry and Society of Indian Defence Manufacturers.

The Belgium Defence Minister underscored the growing strategic partnership between India and the European Union (EU), highlighting the robust dialogue structures developing across maritime security, information security and aerospace. He stated that these institutional frameworks have established India as a trusted partner for the EU.

Commending the dynamism of Indian entrepreneurs, Mr Theo Francken stressed the need to bolster the two militaries in the evolving security environment through joint efforts. “United we stand, divided we fall,” he said.

Highlighting the strategic transformation of India’s defence manufacturing sector, Raksha Rajya Mantri stated that the nation is decisively moving from import dependence to indigenous capability, trusted partnerships, and global competitiveness through initiatives such as Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Make-in-India. “This transformation is outward-facing. Strategic autonomy is best secured through credible, mutually beneficial international collaboration,” he said.

Shri Sanjay Seth emphasised that India and Belgium can leverage their strengths and prioritise collaboration in areas including cyber security, AI-enabled unmanned aerial systems, underwater domain vehicles, and complex weapon systems. He stated that innovation platforms like iDEX and ADITI are engaging start-ups and MSMEs in AI, quantum technologies, military communications, anti-drone systems, and adaptive camouflage, providing “excellent avenues for bilateral R&D and industrialisation”.

Raksha Rajya Mantri pointed out that India’s defence industrial base today combines Defence Public Sector Units, a growing private sector, and over 16,000 MSMEs, with domestic industry delivering advanced capabilities across aerospace, naval and land platforms, defence electronics, cyber security, space technologies, and unmanned systems. Through Department of Defence Production-led measures, India is accelerating capacity building, strengthening value chains, and incentivising technology transfer and co-development, he said.

Shri Sanjay Seth underlined that India has liberalised Foreign Direct Investment in defence up to 74% under the automatic route and up to 100% through the government route to enable partnerships in niche technologies. “The new space policy permits 100% FDI. Dedicated Defence Industrial Corridors in Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh, with further corridors planned in Maharashtra, Assam and other regions, offer competitive incentives and ecosystem support for foreign original equipment manufacturers and partners,” he added.

During the event, multiple MoUs were exchanged towards leveraging Belgian technology with Indian skill and scale. These include pacts between SIDM and Belgian Security & Defence Industry; Larsen & Toubro Limited (India) and Exail Robotics SAS (France) and EXAIL Robotics (Belgium); Kalyani Strategic Systems Ltd (India) and FN Herstal (Belgium); Tembo Classic Engineering Pvt Ltd (India) and Lachaussée SA (Belgium); India Optel Ltd (India) and OIP (Belgium); Krishna Industries Pvt Ltd (India) and Pitagone (Belgium); DGVK Enterprises Private Limited (India) and Sol1 BV (Belgium); and Kalyani Strategic Systems Ltd (India) and Thales Belgium SA and Thales India Pvt Ltd.

In order to encourage and promote healthy plantation practices along the National Highways, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) instituted the ‘Green Highways Excellence Awards’ to recognize best practices in National Highway landscaping & plantation management. The winners of the ‘Green Highways Excellence Awards 2026’ were announced across three categories that included Avenue Plantations, Median Plantations and Plantation in Land Parcels including clover leaves, interchange, toll plazas & service areas. For participation, the entries were opened to NHAI field offices, concessionaires, contractors, government agencies, NGOs and private agencies involved in plantation projects undertaken along the National Highway projects.

Announcing the Winners

Category- I: Avenue Plantations

1st Prize

Project: Six Laning of Chilakaluripet Bypass on NH 16 in Andhra Pradesh, Under RO-Vijayawada

2nd Prize

Project: Eight Lane Vadodara - Kim Expressway, Padra to Vadodara Section of Vadodara - Mumbai Expressway in Gujarat

Under RO-Gandhinagar

3rd Prize

 

Project: Gagariya-Bakhasar section of NH-925 and Satta- Gandhav section of NH-925A, Under RO-Jaipur

Consolation prize

 

Project: Annual Maintenance including Incident Management of Trichy - Karaikudi section of NH-210, NH- 336, 36 & 536, including Trichy Bypass, Under RO-Madurai

 

Category II: Median Plantations:

1st Prize

Project: Four laning of Hyderabad -Yadgiri section of NH 163 km, Under RO-Hyderabad

2nd Prize

Project: Eight Lane Vadodara - Kim Expressway, Sanpa to Padra Section of Vadodara - Mumbai Expressway in Gujarat

Under RO-Gandhinagar

3rd Prize

 

Project: Varanasi Ring Road, Pkg-I, Harahua to Sandaha section of NH-31, Under RO-UP East (Varanasi)

 

Category III: Plantation in Land Parcels:

1st Prize

Project: Jamtha Clover Leaf, Oxygen Bird Park on NH-44 under RO – Nagpur

2nd Prize

Project: Monetization of Public Funded operational National Highway Projects under Tolling. Operation, Maintenance and Transfer (ToT) Bundle-7, NE-lI - land parcels at Duhai Interchange, Under RO-Delhi

3rd Prize

Project: Lucknow-Ayodhya Road and Lucknow Outer Ring Road Intersection Junction - Miyawaki Plantation in Loop Areas,

Under RO- UP West (Lucknow)

 

Nomination and assessment of entries

Award nominations were invited through the NHAI online portal. NHAI received an encouraging response to the NHAI Green Highways Excellence Awards with 86 nominations received from across the country. These comprised 27 nominations for Avenue Plantations, 36 for Median Plantations and 23 for Plantation in Land Parcels.   The nominations included presentations that were supported by geo-tagged photographs, drone videos, site-specific plantation plans and plantation survival-rate data.

Following initial screening, 15 nominations - five in each category were shortlisted for final assessment.  The evaluation was undertaken against a comprehensive assessment framework, with the survival rate of plantations carrying the highest weightage. Other parameters included site-specific plantation action plans, timing of plantation operations, size of pits, quality of planting material, protection measures, implementation as per approved design, species diversity, suitability and use of native species, Special emphasis was laid on quality, sustainability, effectiveness and potential for wider replication across the National Highway network.

The ‘Green Highways Excellence Awards’ was instituted in 2025 by NHAI, as mandated in the Green Highways Policy, 2015. The Awards reinforces NHAI’s commitment to integrating environmental sustainability with the development of the National Highway network across the country.

2306404.title: National Institute of Homoeopathy, Kolkata Celebrates Golden Jubilee
2306404.body_html:
AYUSH
National Institute of Homoeopathy, Kolkata Celebrates Golden Jubilee
Modular Operation Theatre and Centre of Excellence Inaugurated
Advanced infrastructure will strengthen clinical care, research and academic capabilities of NIH Kolkata - Shri. Prataprao Jadhav
Posted On: 03 SEP 2026 5:30PM by PIB Delhi

The National Institute of Homoeopathy (NIH), Kolkata today celebrated its Golden Jubilee, marking 50 years of dedicated service in homoeopathic education, research and patient care. As part of the celebrations, a state-of-the-art Modular Operation Theatre and a Centre of Excellence were inaugurated, significantly strengthening the Institute’s clinical, academic and research infrastructure.

The celebrations were graced by Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush and Minister of State, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare and Shri Sukanta Majumdar, Union Minister of State for Education. Jyotirmay Singh Mahato and Samik Bhattacharya, Members of Parliament, and Sumana Sarkar, MLA, Government of West Bengal, along with Sh. Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, senior officials, faculty members, doctors, students and other stakeholders, were also present on this occasion.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Prataprao Jadhav said that completion of 50 years is a significant milestone in the journey of NIH Kolkata. He said the Golden Jubilee is not only an occasion to acknowledge the Institute’s achievements but also an opportunity to chart its priorities for the coming decades.

The Minister said that the newly inaugurated facilities reflect the Government’s commitment to strengthening Ayush institutions with modern infrastructure, quality education, advanced research capabilities and improved patient-care facilities. He emphasised the need to integrate the strengths of traditional systems of medicine with contemporary technology, research and innovation to address emerging healthcare requirements.

Shri Jadhav also underlined the importance of strengthening homoeopathic education and research and creating greater opportunities for students, researchers and young professionals. He expressed confidence that NIH Kolkata would further consolidate its position as a leading institution in homoeopathic education, research and patient care.

Sukanta Majumdar, Union Minister of State for Education, highlighted NIH Kolkata’s five-decade contribution to education and healthcare. He said the new facilities would further strengthen the Institute as an academic and professional centre and provide enhanced opportunities for learning, training and innovation.

Jyotirmay Singh Mahato, said the expansion of NIH would contribute to improved clinical services and healthcare access for people in Kolkata and surrounding areas.

Rajya Sabha MP Samik Bhattacharya, said the new facilities would enable the Institute to build on its strong institutional foundation and respond effectively to future academic and healthcare requirements.

The newly inaugurated Modular Operation Theatre adds a significant dimension to the Institute’s clinical infrastructure. Designed in accordance with contemporary healthcare requirements and equipped with modern systems, the facility will strengthen NIH Kolkata’s capacity to provide advanced clinical services while supporting training and professional development.

The Centre of Excellence will further enhance the Institute’s capabilities in clinical research, academic development and innovation. It will provide a platform for advancing research, fostering institutional collaborations and creating enhanced opportunities for students, faculty and healthcare professionals.

Dr. Pralay Sharma, Director, NIH Kolkata, said that the new facilities demonstrate NIH’s commitment to strengthening its infrastructure and preparing for the next phase of growth in homoeopathic education, research and patient care.

Ayush Minister Interacts with Students

During his visit to NIH on September 2, 2026, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, along with senior officials of the Ministry of Ayush, also held an extensive interaction with students of the institute to understand their views, concerns and suggestions for further development of homoeopathy.

During the interaction, students highlighted the academic environment and extensive clinical exposure available at NIH, including opportunities to learn from a large and diverse patient base. The Minister also acknowledged the contribution of postgraduate trainees and interns to patient-care activities. The Minister took note of suggestions relating to strengthening institutional infrastructure, including the proposed hospital building, animal house and pharmaceutical analysis laboratory. Issues concerning stipends, housestaffship and the NTET examination were also discussed.

2306390.title: Tiny molecular switch enables nature-inspired biomaterials for self-powered healthcare
2306390.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Tiny molecular switch enables nature-inspired biomaterials for self-powered healthcare
Posted On: 03 SEP 2026 5:12PM by PIB Delhi

A simple yet powerful molecular strategy to create highly efficient piezoelectric biomaterials using peptides—the natural building blocks of proteins could help develop implantable medical devices that power itself using body movements such as heartbeat, breathing, or walking

Piezoelectric materials are special materials that can convert mechanical force, such as pressing, bending, or stretching, into electrical energy. This unique property is used in devices such as pressure sensors, medical ultrasound devices, actuators, and self-powered energy-harvesting systems. However, most commercially available piezoelectric materials are made from ceramics. Although they work well, most conventional piezoelectric materials are brittle, environmentally unfriendly, and often unsuitable for use inside the human body. Scientists have therefore been searching for safer, softer, and biocompatible alternatives.

Researchers from the Centre for Nano and Soft Matter Sciences (CeNS), Bengaluru—an autonomous institute under the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER), Kolkata, and the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR), Bengaluru focused on peptides.

Despite being safe, biodegradable and biocompatible with tissues achieving strong piezoelectric performance from peptide-based materials has remained a long-standing scientific challenge.

Using advanced techniques, the researchers discovered that the key lies not in changing the peptide itself, but in controlling how the peptide molecules assemble. From various microscopic techniques such as atomic force microscopy (AFM) and field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), they found that peptide molecules form nanofibers in water but exhibit no piezoelectric response. However, introducing just one percent of a suitable co-solvent reorganized the molecules into a highly ordered supramolecular arrangement, instantly switching on a strong piezoelectric response without altering the peptide's chemical composition.

This transformation arises because the controlled chiral self-assembly aligns molecular dipoles into a non-centrosymmetric structure—a fundamental structural requirement for piezoelectricity. This elegant molecular approach demonstrates that simply controlling molecular self-assembly can activate or deactivate electrical functionality in biomaterials.

The researchers revealed how subtle molecular reorganization aligns molecular dipoles into a non-centrosymmetric structure that efficiently converts mechanical energy into electricity.

The engineered peptide nanomaterials exhibited a remarkably high piezoelectric coefficient of nearly 30 pm V⁻¹, demonstrating notable performance for a peptide-based material and highlighting their strong potential for next-generation flexible, sustainable, and biocompatible energy-harvesting technologies.

The discovery published in the journal Angewandte Chemie International Edition, provides a new blueprint for designing sustainable functional biomaterials without chemically modifying the molecules themselves. Such materials could one day power wearable electronics, implantable medical sensors, electronic skin, biosensors, and other next-generation healthcare technologies by harvesting energy directly from natural body movements. Beyond biomedical applications, this discovery also offers an environmentally friendly alternative to conventional piezoelectric materials and contributes to the development of sustainable soft electronics.

Fig: Schematic representation of the relation between chiroptical behaviour and piezoelectric response.

The research highlights India's growing strength in supramolecular chemistry, bringing together molecular design, advanced nanoscale characterization, and computational simulations, to solve complex scientific challenges. 

The research was led by Dr Goutam Ghosh at CeNS, together with his PhD scholar Ms Aparna Ramesh, in collaboration with Mr Sarbajit Layek, Prof. Neelanjana Sengupta (IISER Kolkata), and Mr Tarak Nath Das (JNCASR).

Publication Link: https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.3135255

For further details, please contact Dr. Goutam Ghosh at gghosh@cens.res.in

2306381.body_html:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
LOK SABHA SPEAKER GREETS THE PEOPLE ON THE EVE OF JANMASHTAMI
Posted On: 03 SEP 2026 5:01PM by PIB Delhi

Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla has greeted the people on the eve of Janmashtami.

In his message, Shri Birla said:  “Nand ke ghar anand bhayo jai ho Brajpal ki, jai ho Brajpal ki, jai Kanhaiya lal ki, haathi ghoda palki, jai Kanhaiya lal ki …

Heartfelt greetings and best wishes to all the people of the country on the auspicious occasion of Shri Krishna Janmashtami, celebrating the birth of Lord Shri Krishna.

The devotion and love for our revered Lord Shri Krishna are boundless among his countless devotees in India and across the world. The enchanting childhood pastimes of Kanhaiya have been so captivating that lovingly calling him Kanha and Kanhaiya fills the heart with joy and affection. Every mother wishes to shower her children with the same unconditional love and affection that Mother Yashoda bestowed upon Krishna.

Lord Shri Krishna showed us the realities of life. The profound wisdom of the Bhagavad Gita, which Shri Krishna imparted to Arjuna on the battlefield of the Mahabharata, offers timeless guidance on duty, ethics, justice, wisdom, courage, and balance in life. This message has remained a guiding light for humanity for centuries. The Bhagavad Gita is regarded as the soul of India’s philosophical tradition.

Shri Krishna teaches us that no matter how difficult the circumstances may be, the person who stands firmly with truth and righteousness ultimately emerges victorious.

On the auspicious occasion of the birth celebration of Shri Krishna—Govind, Hare Murari, Hey Nath Narayan, Vasudeva—I pray that every home be blessed with happiness and peace, every heart be filled with faith, and every life be infused with renewed energy and enthusiasm.

On Janmashtami, I pray that the blessings of Lord Shri Krishna always remain upon all devotees. May our nation and society continue to move forward on the path of truth, justice, and humanity.

Jai Shri Krishna!”

***

2306374.title: Union Environment Minister reviews Coordinated Efforts by NCR States to tackle Air Pollution
2306374.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2306374.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Union Environment Minister reviews Coordinated Efforts by NCR States to tackle Air Pollution
States crystallise Action-oriented Plans focussing on targeted Stakeholder Engagement and Behavioural Change towards preventing Air Pollution 
SPCBs must focus on Pollution Hotspots, adopt ‘Zero-Tolerance’ policy for Non-conforming Polluting Industries: Shri Bhupender Yadav
Posted On: 03 SEP 2026 4:54PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav today reviewed the comprehensive plans submitted by NCR States, focussing on stakeholder engagement and behavioural change communication to tackle air pollution. The Minister has conducted more than 25 meetings held over the last one year to review individual air quality management plans of the Municipal Bodies in NCR and action taken by them to achieve the targets. This resulted in crystallisation of the individual State action plans, encompassing a range of on-ground activities to tackle the identified sources of air pollution, besides the stakeholder engagement plan reviewed today. 

Chaired a meeting with the Environment Ministers and Secretaries, as well as the Chairpersons and Member Secretaries of the Pollution Control Boards of Delhi, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh, along with the Agriculture Minister and Agriculture Secretary and the Environment Secretary of… pic.twitter.com/2UD0SVur1Q

— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp) September 3, 2026

Welcoming detailed action plans prepared by the NCR State Governments to ensure citizen participation in tackling air pollution, the Minister highlighted specific initiatives undertaken by the States and urged other States to adopt and replicate best practices. Shri Yadav laid special emphasis on strengthening IEC activities and behavioural change communication by taking the campaign to the grassroots and involving all stakeholders. 

The Minister, in his interaction with the NCR State Governments, stressed that coordinated and focused stakeholder engagement is essential to make efforts to tackle air pollution more effective. The Minister reviewed the IEC activities proposed by different States and emphasised that these should be undertaken in a coordinated manner for greater outreach and impact.

Shri Yadav proposed that the Union Ministers for Agriculture, Environment and Urban Development hold meetings with their respective State counterparts to devise coordinated strategies for addressing air pollution. He further emphasised that State Pollution Control Boards must focus on identified air pollution hotspots and prepare practical and effective action plans for their mitigation.

In his interaction with the State authorities, the Minister stressed that “non-conforming polluting industries must be dealt with firmly, following a ‘Zero-Tolerance’ policy”. He also underlined the need to fix responsibility for violations and defaults, with publicising non-conforming stakeholders being adopted as a measure to ensure greater accountability and compliance.

The Minister emphasised that IEC activities alone will not be sufficient, and that effective implementation and enforcement remain critical to tackling air pollution. He informed that a review meeting at the level of the Union Minister would be held in September to assess the progress of initiatives and action taken by the concerned States. He reassured the NCR State Governments that the Government of India would extend full support to their efforts for Air Quality Management.

The meeting was attended by the Secretary (MoEFCC), Chairman, Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM),  and other senior officers from MoEFCC and CAQM. Representation from the State governments included Environment Ministers and Secretaries, as well as the Chairpersons and Member Secretaries of the Pollution Control Boards of Delhi, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh, along with the Agriculture Minister and Agriculture Secretary and the Environment Secretary of Punjab, besides the Additional Chief Secretary and Environment Secretary of Rajasthan.

(Link to State Action Plans: https://caqm.nic.in/landingpage/pages/documents/state-action-plans)

2306369.title: Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and Union Commerce & Industry Minister Piyush Goyal Flag Off New Train Service From CSMT, Mumbai to Sawantwadi Road
2306369.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and Union Commerce & Industry Minister Piyush Goyal Flag Off New Train Service From CSMT, Mumbai to Sawantwadi Road
New Train Service to Strengthen Rail Connectivity Across Konkan Region and Benefit Passengers Across Thane, Ratnagiri, Sindhudurg and Other Important Stations on the Route
More than 370 Special Trains Facilitating Passenger Movement During Ganesh Utsav: Sh. Ashwini Vaishnaw
Posted On: 03 SEP 2026 4:47PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Railways Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw; Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal; Deputy Chief Minister of Maharashtra Shri Eknath Shinde, along with other dignitaries, flagged off the inaugural service of the new train between Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) and Sawantwadi Road today, marking a significant step towards strengthening direct rail connectivity between Mumbai and the Konkan region.

The new train service will provide an important direct rail link between Mumbai and several major towns across the Konkan region, covering a distance of approximately 510 km. With a wide network of stoppages, the service will benefit passengers travelling to and from Raigad, Ratnagiri and Sindhudurg districts.

Railway Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw said the new service would meet the long-standing demand of the people of Mumbai and Konkan. He highlighted that 350 special trains are being operated this year to facilitate the movement of passengers during the festival. He added that arrangements have also been made to increase the number to 370 trains, if required.

Union Minister Shri Piyush Goyal said that the launch of the new daily train service between Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus and Sawantwadi brings immense joy to the people of Maharashtra, particularly during the upcoming Ganesh Utsav. Shri Goyal highlighted that the new service is not merely the launch of another train but an important milestone in the development journey of the Konkan region. Shri Goyal stressed that the new service will help connect lakhs of families by providing a safe, fast and reliable journey between Mumbai and Konkan.

Shri Goyal further said that as freight movement increases on the route, fishermen and other local producers will be able to transport their goods to Mumbai more quickly. He emphasised that improved connectivity will create employment opportunities in Konkan and reduce the need for young people to migrate in search of work.

He also pointed to the benefits for students, employees and families. Shri Goyal said people from Konkan who study or work in Mumbai will be able to maintain closer links with their families and travel more conveniently. He added that Mumbai's higher education opportunities and healthcare services will become more accessible to people in Konkan through improved rail connectivity.

Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Shri Eknath Shinde said the new service is a major gift for the people of Konkan, migrant workers and devotees travelling to their native places during Ganesh Utsav.

Shri Shinde highlighted several major railway achievements, including the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project, Vande Bharat trains and expansion of the railway network across the country. He particularly noted the completion of electrification of the 741-km Konkan Railway route in record time. He said the initiative has enabled a more environment-friendly journey and increased train speeds.

Convenient Timings for Passengers

The train will depart from CSMT at 23:55 hrs and reach Sawantwadi Road at 14:15 hrs the following day. On its return journey, the train will depart from Sawantwadi Road at 17:20 hrs and arrive at CSMT at 06:40 hrs the next morning. The convenient timings will enable passengers to undertake an overnight journey from Mumbai towards Konkan and return to Mumbai early in the morning.

The train will operate daily as Train No. 15087 Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus-Sawantwadi Road Express and Train No. 15088 Sawantwadi Road-Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus Express.

Extensive Connectivity Across Konkan

The service will have stoppages at several important stations, including:

  • Dadar
  • Thane
  • Panvel
  • Pen
  • Roha
  • Mangaon
  • Veer
  • Khed
  • Chiplun
  • Savarda
  • Aravali Road
  • Sangameshwar Road
  • Ratnagiri
  • Adavali
  • Vilavade
  • Rajapur Road
  • Vaibhavwadi Road
  • Nandgaon
  • Kankavli
  • Sindhudurg
  • Kudal
  • Sawantwadi Road

The extensive stoppage pattern will enable passengers to access not only Sawantwadi but also a large number of important towns and localities across the Konkan belt.

Boost to Tourism and Regional Development

The new service is expected to give a further boost to tourism in the Konkan region by improving rail access to destinations in Ratnagiri, Sindhudurg, Kankavli, Kudal and Sawantwadi. Enhanced connectivity will facilitate travel for tourists while creating greater opportunities for local tourism-related businesses and services.

The service will also benefit students, employees, traders, families and other regular travellers by providing an additional dependable rail option between Mumbai and Konkan. Improved movement of people will strengthen economic linkages between Mumbai and the region and support local economic activity.

The train is particularly expected to provide additional travel capacity during festivals, holidays and the tourism season, when passenger demand between Mumbai and Konkan witnesses a substantial increase. The service will operate with an LHB rake, providing passengers with modern and comfortable passenger coaches.

Major Rail Projects to Boost Mumbai’s Capacity and Maharashtra’s Connectivity

Speaking about the Mumbai suburban railway network, Shri Vaishnaw emphasised that several major works are being undertaken to increase capacity and improve passenger services. He said projects worth around ₹18,000 crore are currently underway in Mumbai.

Shri Vaishnaw explained that the Railways is systematically extending platforms designed for 12-coach trains to accommodate 15-coach trains. He said work has already been completed at several locations. He said these initiatives will significantly enhance the capacity of the suburban railway system and improve the daily lives of Mumbaikars.

Shri Vaishnaw further mentioned that the Railways is upgrading the existing signalling system to a modern signalling system to further improve the capacity and efficiency of the Mumbai suburban network.

 

The Railway Minister said 238 new AC local train rakes have also been sanctioned to meet Mumbai's requirement without delay. He announced that delivery of the first AC local train will begin in 2027. Shri Vaishnaw said this will transform the Mumbai suburban railway system with new-generation, air-conditioned local trains, increased capacity and improved passenger comfort.

Turning to the Dedicated Freight Corridors, Shri Vaishnaw said the Eastern and Western Dedicated Freight Corridors are a major strength for the country. He said both freight corridors are now 100 per cent complete.

Shri Vaishnaw also referred to the announcement in the Union Budget of a new East-West Dedicated Freight Corridor. He said that the Railways is designing the new corridor from Dankuni to Surat in a manner that will provide rail connectivity to several areas of Vidarbha, Marathwada and Western Maharashtra, while also connecting the corridor towards Wardha and the port at Nashik, providing a strong network for industrial and rural development in Maharashtra.

On the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail project, Shri Vaishnaw said work is progressing rapidly. He highlighted the construction of an undersea rail tunnel, which will connect BKC and Thane. Two tunnel boring machines, one from Vikhroli and the other from Ghansoli, are currently working on the tunnel.

Rahul Narwekar, Speaker of the Maharashtra Legislative Assembly; Nitesh Rane, Minister of Ports Development and Fisheries, Government of Maharashtra and Ritu Tawde, Mayor of Mumbai, along with other dignitaries were also present on the occasion.

 

 

***

Mahesh Kumar/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj/ Manik Sharma

2306366.title: CCI directs Trustees’ Association of India, IDBI Trusteeship Services Ltd, Axis Trustee Services and SBI CAP Trustee Company to cease and desist from anti-competitive conduct
2306366.body_html:
Competition Commission of India
CCI directs Trustees’ Association of India, IDBI Trusteeship Services Ltd, Axis Trustee Services and SBI CAP Trustee Company to cease and desist from anti-competitive conduct
Posted On: 03 SEP 2026 4:45PM by PIB Delhi

The Competition Commission of India (CCI/the Commission), vide an order dated 02.09.2026 issued under Section 27 of the Competition Act, 2002, (the Act) has directed Trustees’ Association of India (TAI) , IDBI Trusteeship Services Limited, Axis Trustee Services Limited and SBI CAP Trustee Company Limited and their respective individuals liable under Section 48 of the Act, to cease and desist from anti-competitive conduct found to be in violation of Section 3(3)(a) and 3(3)(b) read with Section 3(1) of the Act.

Based on the minutes of meeting of Trustees’ Association of India and certain emails exchanges, the Commission found that the opposite parties fixed the benchmark price, for providing debenture trusteeship services, during the period of FY 2020-21 and 2021-22.

Such collective fixing of minimum price/fee by Trustees’ Association of India, for the provision of debenture trusteeship services, and other follow-on actions prevented independent commercial decision making by the debenture trustees and amounted to cartelisation in terms of the provisions of the Act. Further, CCI found that the conduct also amounts to limiting and controlling the supply/market for provision of said services, as members of Trustees’ Association of India as well non-members were dictated not to provide services to the issuers of debentures below the benchmark fee.

The CCI also found certain officials of Trustees’ Association of India, IDBI Trusteeship Services Limited, Axis Trustee Services Limited and SBI CAP Trustee Company Limited to be liable under Section 48 of the Act. However, in consideration of the mitigating factors, no monetary penalty was imposed on the opposite parties and their individuals.

The order was passed in Case No. 29 of 2021 and a copy of the same is available on the CCI website at www.cci.gov.in.
